# What to Put in an "If Something Happens to Me" Folder

By the Bunker TeamUpdated Oct 24, 2026

An “if something happens to me” folder holds what your family will need in the first days: a one-page letter saying who to call and where things are, your contacts, an account list, how to get into your devices and accounts, copies of key documents, and your wishes. Keep a paper version in one known place and an encrypted digital copy, and tell 2 people where both are.

It’s not a will. It’s the map your family uses to find the will, the policies and everything else, at a time when they won’t be thinking clearly. A good folder saves them weeks.

This is general information, not legal advice. The folder doesn’t decide who inherits anything; your will does. A lawyer, such as James Miller in our examples, can make sure the two agree.

## Page 1: The Letter

Start with one page your family can read in 2 minutes:

  * Who to call first, with numbers: usually your executor and your lawyer.
  * Where the will is, and where the original is if this folder has a copy.
